engagement_affordance: a helper-the-zookeeper framing gives purpose and SDT relatedness; cheerful audiovisual items support dual-coding and lower verbal-only load, keeping young children engaged while they manipulate items in mind
adaptivity_fit: high - list length and number of sort dimensions parameterize difficulty cleanly
tail_discrimination: med/high - two-dimension sorts and longer lists prevent ceiling and reveal strong manipulation capacity
coachability_bias_risk: vocabulary/naming knowledge and touch skill add construct-irrelevant variance; category familiarity (SES); mitigate with picture+audio items, a demo, and culturally common exemplars
advantage_vs_cogat: isolates WM manipulation (not just span) that CogAT does not separate; engaging multimodal delivery yields fuller effort and a truer capacity estimate at the top
source_name: NIH Toolbox Cognition Battery (List Sorting Working Memory Test)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - underlying list-sorting paradigm is public; NIH Toolbox instrument is licensed, build original items

item_format: filter-and-remember game (ACE Filter-style): remember only the target-colored shapes while ignoring distractors, then report their orientation/position after a delay; distractor load parameterized
cognitive_process: selective encoding, WM capacity, distractor suppression
engagement_affordance: a spy/scanner theme (remember the good guys, ignore decoys) creates purposeful flow; immediate hit/miss feedback and rising distractor waves keep effort high while taxing filtering
adaptivity_fit: high - target:distractor ratio and set size are precise difficulty knobs suited to adaptive delivery
tail_discrimination: high - high-distractor loads separate children who filter efficiently from those who overload; low ceiling
coachability_bias_risk: attention/gaming familiarity and motor speed are construct-irrelevant; strategy discovery (chunking) can be coached; standardize tutorial and randomize displays
advantage_vs_cogat: measures attentional filtering into WM, an executive facet CogAT ignores; engagement sustains attention so scores reflect capacity, and telemetry shows encoding strategy
source_name: Anguera/Gazzaley, Neuroscape UCSF, Adaptive Cognitive Evaluation (ACE); validation O'Laughlin et al. (2025), JMIR
reuse_note: adapt_ok - research battery replicating gold-standard tasks; build original stimuli

item_format: running-memory cooking/order game: customers give orders that update; child must serve the last k items in the current order, binding item-to-slot as orders change; running span + binding load scored
cognitive_process: running WM, updating, feature binding, prospective memory
engagement_affordance: role-play as a cook gives SDT autonomy+relatedness and a concrete, meaningful goal (Hirsh-Pasek pillars: active, engaged, meaningful); happy-customer feedback sustains flow while WM is loaded
adaptivity_fit: high - order length, update rate, and number of features (color/shape) parameterize difficulty
tail_discrimination: med - keep binding demands high (multi-feature orders) to avoid ceiling for able young children
coachability_bias_risk: food/vocabulary familiarity, touch skill, and role-play comfort are construct-irrelevant; young-child fatigue; short blocks, demo, and picture cues equalize
advantage_vs_cogat: taps dynamic running-memory and binding CogAT never measures; the playful, concrete task keeps very young children on-task, giving a more valid early-childhood WM read
source_name: Lumsden, Edwards, Lawrence, Coyle & Munafo (2016), Gamification of Cognitive Assessment and Training: A Systematic Review, JMIR Serious Games
reuse_note: adapt_ok - review documents gamified WM-task designs; author original task

item_format: multitask drive-and-respond game (NeuroRacer-style): steer a vehicle on a winding road while responding only to specific signs; single-task and dual-task blocks quantify multitasking cost and speed
cognitive_process: processing speed under interference, divided attention, cognitive control
engagement_affordance: driving with scores and streaks is intrinsically thrilling (flow via speed + tight feedback); the racing frame elicits maximal fast responding without the pressure of a stopwatch on a symbol sheet
adaptivity_fit: high - road speed and signal rate adapt continuously; the paradigm is natively adaptive
tail_discrimination: med/high - dual-task cost (not raw speed) separates strong controllers; include high-load blocks to avoid ceiling
coachability_bias_risk: driving-game familiarity and device input latency are construct-irrelevant; sex/SES exposure gaps; standardize hardware and give an adaptation block before scoring
advantage_vs_cogat: yields multitasking-cost and RT-distribution metrics CogAT cannot; the exciting frame secures full-speed effort, so processing speed is measured at true ceiling rather than under boredom
source_name: Anguera et al. (2013), Video game training enhances cognitive control (NeuroRacer), Nature
reuse_note: adapt_ok - published paradigm; build an original multitask racer

item_format: speeded same/different game (Pattern Comparison style): two figures flash; tap 'same' or 'different' as fast as possible for as many trials as possible in a fixed window; score = correct responses per unit time
cognitive_process: perceptual/comparison speed, rapid visual discrimination
engagement_affordance: a beat-the-clock arcade with rising combo meter creates flow and a personal-best competence loop (SDT); the playful timer feels like a challenge, not evaluative threat, so children push their true speed
adaptivity_fit: high - figure similarity and time window parameterize; huge clonable stimulus pool
tail_discrimination: med - processing-speed tasks can compress at the top for able kids; add subtle differences and a hard block to spread the tail
coachability_bias_risk: tap latency/motor speed, device responsiveness, and gaming reflexes are core construct-irrelevant variance; require identical hardware, a motor-only baseline, and warm-up trials
advantage_vs_cogat: clean RT/throughput metrics with practice-curve telemetry beyond CogAT's paper speed proxies; game framing maximizes effort so speed is not under-estimated by disengagement
source_name: NIH Toolbox Cognition Battery (Pattern Comparison Processing Speed Test)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - perceptual-speed paradigm is public; build original stimuli

item_format: target-detection vigilance game (continuous-performance/TOVA-style): respond to frequent targets and withhold to rare non-targets (or vice versa) over several minutes; RT, RT variability, omissions and commissions scored
cognitive_process: sustained attention, vigilance, response consistency, inhibitory control
engagement_affordance: a friendly catch-the-critters loop with gentle audio rewards fights the boredom that normally sinks vigilance tasks; light gamification (Lumsden) preserves motivation so the vigilance decrement reflects attention, not disinterest
adaptivity_fit: med - duration and target rate parameterize, but vigilance needs sustained blocks (not short adaptive items) for valid signal
tail_discrimination: med - low RT variability and few lapses mark strong attenders; ceiling possible for brief tasks, so use longer blocks
coachability_bias_risk: motor speed, device latency, and momentary fatigue/motivation are construct-irrelevant; over-gamification can distort the vigilance signal; balance rewards and standardize timing
advantage_vs_cogat: CogAT has no sustained-attention measure; continuous telemetry (RT variability, lapse timing) reveals attentional stability, and modest game rewards keep able children engaged enough to show true vigilance
source_name: Kollins et al. (2020), STARS-ADHD RCT of AKL-T01 (primary outcome TOVA continuous-performance test), Lancet Digital Health
reuse_note: describe_only - TOVA/AKL-T01 are commercial; the continuous-performance paradigm is public, build an original vigilance task

item_format: decode-the-message game (symbol-substitution/coding style): use a shown symbol-to-key legend to translate as many symbols as possible before time runs out; speed + accuracy scored, legend refreshed each block
cognitive_process: associative processing speed, visual scanning, incidental learning
engagement_affordance: a secret-agent decoder theme gives purpose and SDT competence; unlocking a hidden message is a concrete reward that sustains fast effort where a plain coding sheet would feel tedious
adaptivity_fit: med/high - legend size and time window parameterize; watch incidental-learning confound as blocks repeat
tail_discrimination: med - speeded coding can ceiling for able kids; use larger legends and novel symbols to extend the top
coachability_bias_risk: motor/tap speed, device latency, and legend-memorization strategy are construct-irrelevant; refresh legends, standardize hardware, and provide a motor baseline
advantage_vs_cogat: provides throughput and learning-slope telemetry beyond CogAT paper speed items; the decoder narrative secures maximal effort so speed reflects capacity, not compliance
source_name: Lumsden, Edwards, Lawrence, Coyle & Munafo (2016), Gamification of Cognitive Assessment and Training: A Systematic Review, JMIR Serious Games
reuse_note: adapt_ok - coding/substitution paradigm is public; build original symbols/legend

item_format: flanker fish game: tap the direction the center fish faces while flanking fish point the same (congruent) or opposite (incongruent) way; congruency effect, accuracy and RT scored
cognitive_process: inhibitory control, selective attention, conflict resolution
engagement_affordance: a cute underwater theme and swipe-the-fish interaction are age-perfect and low-anxiety; congruent 'easy win' trials build SDT competence, keeping young children engaged through the harder incongruent conflict trials
adaptivity_fit: med - congruency and pace vary but the core contrast (congruent vs incongruent) is fixed; limited difficulty range
tail_discrimination: low/med - flanker effects compress in high-ability children (near ceiling); useful for screening/executive profiling more than top-tail ranking
coachability_bias_risk: motor/tap speed, device latency, and simple practice are construct-irrelevant; young-child impulsivity confounds; use demo, forgiving timing, and many trials to stabilize the congruency estimate
advantage_vs_cogat: CogAT omits inhibitory control; the game yields a conflict-cost metric and keeps 5-6 year olds attentive, but its low ceiling means it complements rather than extends CogAT's high tail
source_name: NIH Toolbox Cognition Battery (Flanker Inhibitory Control and Attention Test)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - Eriksen flanker paradigm is public; build original art

item_format: card-sort switch game (Dimensional Change Card Sort style): sort cards by color, then the rule switches to shape (then mixed); switch cost, accuracy and RT scored
cognitive_process: cognitive flexibility, set shifting, rule representation
engagement_affordance: a sort-for-the-characters game with cheerful confirmation animations gives immediate feedback and SDT competence; the rule-switch is framed as a fun twist, reducing the frustration that derails young children
adaptivity_fit: med - number of dimensions and switch frequency parameterize; core paradigm has limited spread
tail_discrimination: low/med - designed to differentiate early executive development; ceilings for older able children, so best for K-2 profiling
coachability_bias_risk: drag skill, comprehension of instructions, and impulsivity are construct-irrelevant; verbal rule load; equalize with picture rules, demo, and practice sorts
advantage_vs_cogat: measures set-shifting CogAT ignores; playful delivery keeps young children compliant so early executive function is validly captured, complementing CogAT's reasoning focus
source_name: NIH Toolbox Cognition Battery (Dimensional Change Card Sort Test)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - DCCS paradigm is public; build original cards

item_format: crystal-mover puzzle (Tower of London/Hanoi style): rearrange colored balls/crystals across pegs to match a goal in the fewest moves within a move limit; planning time, first-move latency, moves-over-minimum, and rule violations scored
cognitive_process: planning, look-ahead, subgoaling, impulse control
engagement_affordance: a wizard-tower theme and star ratings for efficient solutions create SDT competence and replay motivation; the visible move counter turns planning into a satisfying optimization game rather than a clinical task
adaptivity_fit: high - peg count, goal depth, and move limits give a clean, calibrated difficulty ladder for CAT
tail_discrimination: high - moves-over-minimum and planning latency on deep problems sharply separate strong planners; low ceiling with hard configs
coachability_bias_risk: puzzle familiarity, drag precision, and learned heuristics are construct-irrelevant; repeated configurations can be memorized; randomize goals and provide tutorial + practice
advantage_vs_cogat: measures planning/executive function CogAT does not; first-move-latency and efficiency telemetry expose whether a child plans ahead or acts impulsively, adding process insight at the tail
source_name: Shallice (1982), Specific impairments of planning (Tower of London), Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
reuse_note: adapt_ok - classic public paradigm (cf. Tower of Hanoi); author original puzzles

item_format: go/no-go stop game: tap fast for 'go' targets but withhold on rare 'stop' signals (or stop-signal variant with a delayed cue); commission errors, RT, and stopping accuracy scored
cognitive_process: response inhibition, impulse control, prepotent-response suppression
engagement_affordance: a whack-fast-but-freeze mechanic is inherently playful and giggly for young children; frequent go-trial success builds SDT competence and flow, keeping them engaged through the harder inhibition demands
adaptivity_fit: med - go:no-go ratio and stop-signal delay parameterize; adaptive staircase possible on SSD
tail_discrimination: low/med - inhibition compresses at the top; more useful for impulse-control profiling and screening than high-tail ranking
coachability_bias_risk: motor speed, device latency, and a wait-and-see strategy inflate scores as construct-irrelevant variance; young-child motivation swings; standardize timing, demo, and monitor strategic slowing
advantage_vs_cogat: adds an impulse-control dimension CogAT lacks; the game keeps toddlers/early learners on-task so inhibition is measured validly, complementing reasoning scores
source_name: Anguera/Gazzaley, Neuroscape UCSF, Adaptive Cognitive Evaluation (ACE)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - go/no-go and stop-signal paradigms are public; build original stimuli

item_format: branching social scenarios (Zoo U-style stealth SEL): navigate school-like situations (join a game at recess, resolve a conflict) by choosing actions; six skills (impulse control, emotion regulation, empathy, communication, cooperation, social initiation) inferred from choices and timing
cognitive_process: social problem solving, emotion recognition, perspective taking
engagement_affordance: a story-driven virtual school with a helpful principal character gives SDT relatedness and autonomy; children reveal authentic social choices in-role, which lowers social-desirability bias versus a questionnaire
adaptivity_fit: med - scenes author to skill and difficulty but scoring needs validated algorithms per skill; not a quick CAT pool
tail_discrimination: med - strong social reasoners choose adaptive strategies consistently; graded scenario difficulty spreads scores but ceilings exist
coachability_bias_risk: reading/language load, cultural norms of 'appropriate' behavior (DIF risk), and story-comprehension differences are construct-irrelevant; use audio narration, culturally varied scenes, and validation across groups
advantage_vs_cogat: measures SEL competence entirely outside CogAT's scope; performance-based choices under engagement give a truer social profile than self-report, broadening who is identified as gifted
source_name: DeRosier & Thomas (2017), Establishing the criterion validity of Zoo U's game-based SE skills assessment, Journal of Applied Developmental Psychology
reuse_note: adapt_ok - published SEL GBA paradigm; author original scenarios

item_format: narrative emotion-reading game (Crystals of Kaydor-style): as a robot on an alien world, identify and gauge the intensity of facial emotions to complete social quests; empathic-accuracy and calibration scored from choices
cognitive_process: emotion recognition, empathic accuracy, affective perspective taking
engagement_affordance: an immersive sci-fi narrative provides implicit motivation to take others' perspectives and strong SDT relatedness; emotional storytelling drives engagement so children practice reading affect naturally, not as a quiz
adaptivity_fit: med - emotion subtlety and context parameterize difficulty; authoring rich narrative content is costly
tail_discrimination: med - fine intensity discriminations separate highly empathic children; ceiling for basic-emotion recognition, so include subtle blends
coachability_bias_risk: cultural display-rule differences and facial-stimulus representativeness are DIF/construct-irrelevant risks; reading load; use diverse faces, audio, and cross-group validation
advantage_vs_cogat: assesses socio-emotional talent CogAT cannot; narrative engagement yields authentic empathic behavior and process data (accuracy + calibration) that broadens the definition of giftedness
source_name: Kral et al. (2018), Neural correlates of video game empathy training (Crystals of Kaydor), npj Science of Learning
reuse_note: adapt_ok - published research game paradigm; build an original emotion-reading narrative

item_format: stealth persistence measure: within any puzzle game, embed some very hard/unsolvable items and log time-on-task, retries after failure, and voluntary re-attempts; persistence estimated from telemetry (not a scored 'answer')
cognitive_process: persistence, frustration tolerance, effort regulation
engagement_affordance: because the game is intrinsically fun (flow), children choose to keep trying, revealing genuine persistence; SDT autonomy (free to retry or move on) makes the behavior authentic rather than compliance-driven
adaptivity_fit: med - persistence probes embed into any level, but require careful difficulty calibration so 'hard' is equal across children
tail_discrimination: med - time-on-hard-items and retry counts separate persistent children, but engagement/interest confounds must be modeled
coachability_bias_risk: intrinsic interest in the specific game, prior exposure, and fatigue are construct-irrelevant; a child may persist in a liked game and quit a disliked one; use neutral-appeal content and multiple probes
advantage_vs_cogat: captures a noncognitive predictor (persistence) CogAT cannot; behavioral telemetry under engagement is far more valid than self-report and identifies effortful children who may underperform on timed tests
source_name: Ventura & Shute (2013), The validity of a game-based assessment of persistence, Computers in Human Behavior
reuse_note: adapt_ok - published GBA-of-persistence method; embed original probes

item_format: open-ended sandbox creativity probe: score solution originality and fluency in a design/physics sandbox (e.g., number of distinct working solutions, unusual-but-valid approaches) via stealth indicators
cognitive_process: divergent thinking, creative problem solving, fluency/originality
engagement_affordance: maximal SDT autonomy (make it your way) plus non-judgmental exploration lowers evaluation apprehension, which is essential for divergent thinking; flow in the sandbox elicits generative behavior a test cannot
adaptivity_fit: low/med - creativity is hard to standardize and score reliably; needs rubric/telemetry models and human-in-the-loop calibration
tail_discrimination: med/high - originality metrics can surface exceptional creative talent, but reliability of creativity scoring is a known limitation
coachability_bias_risk: domain familiarity, prior sandbox exposure, and scorer subjectivity are construct-irrelevant/DIF risks; evaluation anxiety suppresses creativity; use open prompts, warm-up, and multi-rater or telemetry-based scoring
advantage_vs_cogat: assesses creativity CogAT wholly omits; a low-stakes engaging sandbox unlocks divergent output and process telemetry, widening identification beyond convergent reasoning
source_name: Shute & Ventura (2013), Stealth Assessment (MIT Press)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - stealth measures of creativity/persistence described; build original probes

item_format: balloon-pump decision game (BART-style, as in pymetrics): pump a balloon to bank points but a pop loses the round's points; risk tolerance, learning, and consistency inferred from behavior (no right answer)
cognitive_process: decision making under uncertainty, risk calibration, reward learning
engagement_affordance: tension between greed and caution creates a gambling-like flow and immediate consequence feedback; because there is no correct answer, children act naturally, which reduces evaluative anxiety and reveals authentic tendencies
adaptivity_fit: med - reward/variance parameters vary but this profiles a trait, not an ability level; not a difficulty-laddered CAT
tail_discrimination: low/med - measures a behavioral tendency (risk) rather than max ability, so 'tail' framing is weak; useful for profiling
coachability_bias_risk: prior exposure to the task, numeracy, and understanding of the payoff structure are construct-irrelevant; strategy is coachable once known; treat as trait profiling and validate for fairness/DIF
advantage_vs_cogat: adds a decision/behavioral dimension CogAT ignores; behavior-based (not self-report) data under engagement is harder to fake, but it complements rather than extends CogAT's ability tail
source_name: pymetrics (now Harver), neuroscience mini-games for talent assessment (overview: University of Oxford Careers Service)
reuse_note: describe_only - proprietary commercial assessment; describe the BART mechanic/construct mapping only (BART paradigm itself is public)

item_format: dot-comparison herd game (Panamath-style ANS): two arrays of animals/dots flash; tap the more numerous set; ratio (Weber fraction) adapts; perceptual controls on size/area; accuracy and RT scored
cognitive_process: approximate number sense, nonsymbolic magnitude discrimination
engagement_affordance: quick which-herd-is-bigger taps with cheerful feedback are effortless and pre-verbal, ideal for young or low-language children; flow from fast rounds keeps them going, and no reading lowers anxiety and stereotype threat
adaptivity_fit: high - numerical ratio is a precise difficulty parameter (Weber fraction staircase); huge auto-generated stimulus pool
tail_discrimination: high - finer ratios separate strong number sense; notably, ANS acuity correlates with math even among mathematically gifted adolescents, so it discriminates at the top
coachability_bias_risk: visual/perceptual cues (area, density) can be exploited as construct-irrelevant variance if not controlled; touch speed; strictly control perceptual confounds, standardize timing, and give practice
advantage_vs_cogat: measures a nonverbal number sense CogAT's quantitative items do not isolate, with minimal language/coaching load; engaging, culture-fair delivery elicits full effort and separates the high-math tail
source_name: Halberda, Mazzocco & Feigenson (2008), Individual differences in non-verbal number acuity correlate with maths achievement, Nature (Panamath)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - Panamath is a free research tool; build an original dot-comparison game

item_format: number-line placement / linear-board race: drag a numeral to its position on a 0-10/0-100/0-1000 line, or advance a token on a linear board by counting; linearity/percent-absolute-error and count-on behavior scored
cognitive_process: numerical magnitude representation, symbolic-to-spatial mapping
engagement_affordance: a friendly race/hop-to-the-spot mechanic makes abstract magnitude concrete and playful (dual coding); each placement gives instant visual feedback and SDT competence, sustaining practice young children resist on worksheets
adaptivity_fit: high - range and target values parameterize a large calibrated pool; strong CAT fit
tail_discrimination: med - basic ranges ceiling for able children; extend to larger ranges/fractions and tighter tolerance to spread the tail
coachability_bias_risk: numeral familiarity, drag precision, and prior number-line instruction are construct-irrelevant/coachable; equalize with demo, forgiving hit tolerance, and randomized targets
advantage_vs_cogat: captures magnitude representation (a core predictor of math achievement) with placement telemetry beyond CogAT's multiple-choice quantitative items; engagement yields fuller effort from young children
source_name: Siegler (2016), Magnitude knowledge: the common core of numerical development (linear number-board games; Siegler & Ramani), review
reuse_note: reuse_verbatim - number-line estimation is a public paradigm; reuse/author freely

item_format: adaptive number game (The Number Race-style): choose the larger quantity across nonsymbolic, spoken, and written formats, then move along a racetrack; difficulty adapts on distance, deadline, and symbolic ratio to hold ~75% success
cognitive_process: symbolic/nonsymbolic magnitude, number-space mapping, early arithmetic
engagement_affordance: multi-format reinforcement plus a racetrack payoff links number to space and keeps success near 75%, the sweet spot for flow and SDT competence; adaptivity prevents both boredom and defeat, sustaining effort
adaptivity_fit: high - multidimensional adaptive algorithm (distance, speed, symbolic ratio) is native to the design
tail_discrimination: med - designed for remediation/low end; raise symbolic ratios, add arithmetic and tighter deadlines to discriminate the high end
coachability_bias_risk: numeral/word knowledge, language of narration, and prior schooling are construct-irrelevant/coachable; standardize language, provide audio, and validate across language backgrounds
advantage_vs_cogat: integrates nonsymbolic-to-symbolic mapping and speed with adaptive engagement CogAT lacks; the always-appropriately-hard loop elicits sustained effort, giving a truer early-numeracy read
source_name: Wilson, Dehaene et al. (2006), Principles underlying the design of The Number Race, Behavioral and Brain Functions
reuse_note: adapt_ok - freely available research software; adapt the adaptive-comparison design

item_format: build-the-number puzzle: compose target quantities from base-ten blocks (ones/tens/hundreds) or coins, and decompose/regroup to solve; efficiency of grouping and regrouping strategy scored via telemetry
cognitive_process: place-value understanding, composition/decomposition, quantitative reasoning
engagement_affordance: manipulating physical-feeling blocks (embodied/concrete, then fading to abstract) gives tactile flow and SDT competence; a shopkeeper/treasury theme adds purpose so children explore regrouping instead of rote answering
adaptivity_fit: high - target magnitude and required regrouping depth parameterize a calibrated pool
tail_discrimination: med/high - efficient regrouping and flexible decomposition on large numbers separate strong quantitative reasoners
coachability_bias_risk: prior base-ten instruction and drag skill are construct-irrelevant/coachable; currency/unit familiarity (culture); use demo, culture-neutral tokens, and randomized targets
advantage_vs_cogat: reveals place-value reasoning process (strategy, regrouping) that CogAT's answer-only quantitative items hide; concrete engaging manipulation elicits fuller reasoning from young children
source_name: Siegler (2016), Magnitude knowledge: the common core of numerical development, review
reuse_note: adapt_ok - grounded in numerical-development research; author original manipulatives task

item_format: find-the-word quest (Picture Vocabulary style): hear a spoken word and tap the matching picture from four options; difficulty scales by word frequency/abstractness; low reading load
cognitive_process: receptive vocabulary, word-meaning mapping, verbal knowledge
engagement_affordance: a collect-the-words adventure with audio and pictures uses dual coding to keep it accessible to pre-readers; friendly narration and rewards give SDT competence, lowering the anxiety of a verbal test
adaptivity_fit: high - word frequency/difficulty give a clean IRT-calibrated CAT pool; large item bank
tail_discrimination: med/high - include rare/abstract words to avoid ceiling and separate strong verbal-knowledge children
coachability_bias_risk: language exposure (SES, home language) is major construct-irrelevant variance and DIF risk; picture cultural representativeness; validate across groups and provide clear audio
advantage_vs_cogat: delivers verbal knowledge assessment with audio (not reading), reducing decoding confounds CogAT verbal items carry; engaging format keeps young/EL children trying, giving a fairer verbal estimate
source_name: NIH Toolbox Cognition Battery (Picture Vocabulary Test)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - receptive-vocabulary picture-selection paradigm is public; author original items

item_format: interactive story-quest: an audio/animated narrative pauses for choices and comprehension/inference probes (who wanted what, why, what happens next); inference and integration scored from choices and re-listens
cognitive_process: listening comprehension, inference, narrative integration
engagement_affordance: a branching story the child helps steer delivers SDT autonomy and relatedness with characters; narrative transportation sustains attention so comprehension is measured during genuine engagement, not a dry passage
adaptivity_fit: med - probes author to difficulty (literal vs inferential) but rich narrative content is expensive to produce/clone
tail_discrimination: med/high - deep-inference and integrative probes separate strong comprehenders; ceiling low if inference load is high
coachability_bias_risk: vocabulary/background knowledge and language of narration are construct-irrelevant/DIF risks; memory load confound; use audio, replays, culturally varied stories, and cross-group validation
advantage_vs_cogat: assesses oral comprehension/inference without reading-decoding barriers CogAT verbal items impose; engagement elicits real comprehension effort, broadening who demonstrates verbal talent
source_name: Shute & Ventura (2013), Stealth Assessment (MIT Press)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - stealth-assessment-in-narrative principles; author original stories/probes

item_format: argument-battle game (Argubot Academy style): build claims and match evidence to support positions, then 'battle' opposing arguments; quality of claim-evidence links scored via Evidence-Centered game Design against argumentation progressions
cognitive_process: verbal reasoning, argumentation, claim-evidence evaluation
engagement_affordance: a Pokemon-like battle frame (master the mechanics of argument with the passion of collecting) gives strong SDT competence and relatedness; the battle stakes turn abstract reasoning into a compelling, low-anxiety contest
adaptivity_fit: med - scenarios and evidence sets author to difficulty but need ECgD evidence models; not a quick CAT pool
tail_discrimination: high - constructing strong multi-part arguments and rebutting weak ones separates strong verbal reasoners; open construction lowers ceiling
coachability_bias_risk: reading/language load, topic background knowledge, and argument-format coaching are construct-irrelevant/DIF risks; use audio support, familiar topics, and validate across groups
advantage_vs_cogat: measures generative verbal reasoning/argumentation CogAT (recognition-only) cannot; engagement and construction telemetry reveal reasoning quality and true high-end verbal talent
source_name: GlassLab/ETS, Mars Generation One: Argubot Academy (Evidence-Centered game Design; CBAL argumentation progressions)
reuse_note: describe_only - ECgD/CBAL method reusable; Argubot Academy is a released title, build an original argument game

item_format: word-building/anagram treasure game: form as many valid words as possible from given letters, or spell target words, under a time budget; word count/length and lexical-access speed scored
cognitive_process: orthographic-lexical access, vocabulary breadth, verbal fluency
engagement_affordance: a race to unlock treasure by spelling words creates a personal-best flow loop and SDT competence; letter-tile play is tactile and low-stakes, encouraging attempts where a spelling test would provoke anxiety
adaptivity_fit: med/high - letter sets and time budgets parameterize; scoring against a lexicon is automatable
tail_discrimination: med/high - rare/long words and high fluency separate strong verbal children; open production lowers ceiling
coachability_bias_risk: spelling instruction, vocabulary exposure (SES/home language), and keyboard/tile familiarity are construct-irrelevant/DIF risks; standardize input, allow audio, and validate across language backgrounds
advantage_vs_cogat: captures productive verbal fluency and lexical access CogAT does not assess; engaging production elicits effortful output and reveals verbal breadth beyond recognition items
source_name: Lumsden, Edwards, Lawrence, Coyle & Munafo (2016), Gamification of Cognitive Assessment and Training: A Systematic Review, JMIR Serious Games
reuse_note: adapt_ok - review documents gamified verbal tasks; author original word game

item_format: PRECEDENT/METHOD: stealth assessment via Evidence-Centered Design - embed competency, evidence, and task models with Bayesian-network scoring so gameplay telemetry (not explicit test items) yields valid ability estimates
cognitive_process: evidence-based inference over process data (any target construct)
engagement_affordance: the whole point of stealth assessment is that assessment is invisible and woven into play, preserving flow and intrinsic motivation (SDT) so children never disengage from a 'test' - the enabling method for every row here
adaptivity_fit: high - ECD separates the evidence model from tasks, enabling adaptive task selection and reusable scoring across games
tail_discrimination: high - process telemetry captures strategy and efficiency, discriminating strong reasoners beyond correct/incorrect outcomes
coachability_bias_risk: validity hinges on modeling construct-irrelevant variance (game familiarity, device, motor) explicitly; requires validation against external measures and fairness/DIF checks before use
advantage_vs_cogat: the core thesis: engagement keeps effort maximal (truer tail), and rich process evidence reveals HOW children reason - dimensions CogAT's outcome-only items cannot provide
source_name: Shute & Ventura (2013), Stealth Assessment (MIT Press); Mislevy, Steinberg & Almond (2003), ECD
reuse_note: adapt_ok - foundational method; apply ECD to build validated evidence models

item_format: PRECEDENT/REVIEW: systematic review of 33 studies / 31 gamified cognitive tasks - documents that working memory and executive function are the most common targets, gamified tests usually validate, and engagement boosts motivation (with mixed measurement caveats)
cognitive_process: cross-construct (WM, EF, attention, speed) via gamified paradigms
engagement_affordance: synthesizes seven documented reasons researchers gamify - chiefly engagement/motivation and reduced attrition/anxiety - the empirical backbone for the engagement-to-truer-measurement thesis in this shard
adaptivity_fit: high - reviews adaptive/parameterizable designs, but warns mixed-domain measurement can muddy the target construct
tail_discrimination: med - notes gamification aids motivation but can add construct-irrelevant variance; careful design needed to preserve discrimination
coachability_bias_risk: the review itself flags that game elements may introduce construct-irrelevant variance and that validation is essential - directly the coachability/novelty concern
advantage_vs_cogat: evidence base that careful gamification yields engaging yet scientifically valid assessment; supports engagement-driven fuller effort while cautioning that game skill must be separated from the target ability
source_name: Lumsden, Edwards, Lawrence, Coyle & Munafo (2016), Gamification of Cognitive Assessment and Training: A Systematic Review, JMIR Serious Games
reuse_note: adapt_ok - reference review guiding design and validation choices

item_format: PRECEDENT/INSTRUMENT: Adaptive Cognitive Evaluation (ACE) - a mobile, adaptive battery of 15 game-like tasks (flanker, Stroop, task-switch, filter/WM, spatial span, sustained attention) that replicate gold-standard EF measures for ages 7-107
cognitive_process: executive function: attention, working memory, goal management, flexibility
engagement_affordance: immersive graphics, video tutorials, and motivating feedback with adaptive difficulty keep the same tasks engaging across the lifespan (flow via calibrated challenge), a working model for kid-friendly EF assessment
adaptivity_fit: high - built around adaptive algorithms per task; the reference design for adaptive game-based EF measurement
tail_discrimination: med/high - adaptive staircases push able children toward their limits, extending the measurable tail on several EF tasks
coachability_bias_risk: device/motor and task-familiarity effects are construct-irrelevant; standardized tutorials and adaptive calibration are used to reduce them - a template for equalizing novelty
advantage_vs_cogat: provides a validated adaptive EF battery CogAT lacks; engagement and adaptivity elicit full effort and yield process metrics (RT, adaptation) beyond CogAT outcomes
source_name: Neuroscape UCSF, Adaptive Cognitive Evaluation (ACE); validation O'Laughlin et al. (2025), JMIR
reuse_note: adapt_ok - research battery; model original tasks on its adaptive design

item_format: PRECEDENT/INSTRUMENT: NIH Toolbox Cognition Battery - tablet-delivered, partly adaptive tasks covering executive function, attention, working memory, episodic memory, processing speed, and language, with an Early Childhood battery for ages 3-6
cognitive_process: multi-construct cognition (fluid + crystallized composites)
engagement_affordance: child-friendly animated tasks with clear feedback and short durations reduce test fatigue/anxiety versus paper batteries; a documented model for engaging, standardized multi-construct measurement in young children
adaptivity_fit: high - several subtests are adaptive and normed 3-85+, showing feasibility of a calibrated K-8 battery
tail_discrimination: med - many subtests target normal-range development and can ceiling for gifted children; fluid tasks (e.g., visual reasoning) extend higher
coachability_bias_risk: language load (crystallized tasks), device/motor, and instruction comprehension are construct-irrelevant/DIF risks; standardized administration and norms address some but require gifted-range validation
advantage_vs_cogat: demonstrates a validated tablet battery spanning constructs CogAT under-weights (WM, EF, speed, episodic memory); engaging delivery supports fuller effort, though top-tail ceilings must be addressed

item_format: PRECEDENT/PRODUCT: EndeavorRx (AKL-T01, from Project EVO/NeuroRacer lineage) - an adaptive perceptual-motor navigate-and-target game; FDA-cleared to improve attention in children 8-12, validated against the TOVA continuous-performance test
cognitive_process: selective/sustained attention, cognitive control, processing speed
engagement_affordance: immersive art, music, and storytelling wrap a demanding attention task so children willingly do many trials; a proof point that engaging design sustains effort on otherwise dull attention paradigms (flow + reward)
adaptivity_fit: high - continuously adaptive interference/difficulty; native adaptive engine
tail_discrimination: low/med - built as a clinical treatment for attention deficits, not to rank high-ability children; tail use would need re-purposing
coachability_bias_risk: device/motor skill, gaming familiarity, and practice are construct-irrelevant; as a therapeutic it targets deficits, so gifted-range discrimination is unproven; validation required before selection use
advantage_vs_cogat: demonstrates that an adaptive game can validly index attention (vs TOVA) with high engagement - a capability CogAT lacks - though as a proprietary treatment it is a precedent, not a reusable item

item_format: PRECEDENT/PRODUCT: commercial cognitive-training game suites (Lumosity, Peak, CogniFit) - mini-games mapped to memory, attention, speed, flexibility, and problem solving with in-app scoring and progress tracking
cognitive_process: mixed (working memory, attention, speed, flexibility)
engagement_affordance: polished, habit-forming loops (streaks, daily challenges, progress graphs) are strong engagement models; but note these are training/entertainment products, not validated selection assessments - engagement design to emulate, claims to avoid
adaptivity_fit: med - games adapt difficulty, but scores are not psychometrically calibrated ability estimates
tail_discrimination: low - designed for broad consumer training, not high-ability discrimination; scores confounded by practice
coachability_bias_risk: heavy practice/familiarity effects and self-selection are construct-irrelevant; transfer claims are contested (Lumos Labs settled a 2016 US FTC action over unsupported cognitive-benefit advertising) - a caution against overclaiming training-to-ability
advantage_vs_cogat: illustrates best-in-class engagement mechanics that could raise effort/reduce anxiety versus CogAT, but as unvalidated proprietary training they are precedents for design only, not measurement

item_format: child sees two side-by-side patterns and taps a smiley (same) or frowny (different) face as fast as possible for about 90 seconds
cognitive_process: perceptual comparison speed plus sustained attention (a simple choice reaction time)
engagement_affordance: non-verbal smiley/frowny taps already feel game-like for young children; add a countdown and combo meter, but score accuracy and consistency (not peak speed) so it never rewards impulsive tapping
adaptivity_fit: high - stimuli vary by color or add/remove an element; difficulty via similarity and item count; speed is a continuous measure, less classic CAT
tail_discrimination: low - items are deliberately easy with errors minimized, so it captures speed not ceiling ability; weak at separating the gifted tail
coachability_bias_risk: moderate-to-large practice effect (about 5.5 points over one week in norming); touchscreen/motor latency and attention/ADHD strongly move scores
advantage_vs_cogat: weak as a STANDALONE gifted signal; its value is collateral evidence of engagement/effort and response CONSISTENCY (slowest-response/lapse rate), which tracks ability better than peak speed; CogAT gives no timing or process data

item_format: decide if two simple figures are the same or different when they differ by one feature (a color or an added dot) and tap YES or NO quickly

engagement_affordance: quick same/different rounds suit a fast-paced card-flip mini-game; keep a streak bonus for accurate calls rather than raw speed
adaptivity_fit: high - trivially templated; difficulty scales with feature similarity and number of features
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - easy ceiling; only the hardest similarity levels show any high-end spread
coachability_bias_risk: large practice effects; strategy and familiarity transfer quickly; device latency confounds timing
advantage_vs_cogat: as a standalone gifted signal it is weak; useful mainly as an engagement/effort check and for response consistency; CogAT captures reasoning but no processing efficiency

engagement_affordance: length tiers (3/6/9 digits) map naturally onto level-ups; reward correct calls per minute, not fastest single tap

tail_discrimination: low-to-med - longer strings add a small working-memory demand that gives slightly more high-end spread than pure pattern matching
coachability_bias_risk: practice and chunking strategies inflate scores; numeracy familiarity and device speed confound

item_format: in each row of six numbers, find and mark the two that are identical, completing as many rows as possible within a 3-minute limit (early rows use small numbers/shapes for young children)

tail_discrimination: low - a perceptual-speed test, not a reasoning test; ceilings quickly and does not stretch the gifted tail
coachability_bias_risk: practice effects; fine-motor and visual-tracking demands add construct-irrelevant variance for the youngest children

item_format: Two simultaneous streams (a moving square position and a spoken letter); child responds separately when either stream matches n items back - dual-modality updating
cognitive_process: simultaneous visuospatial and auditory updating with divided attention
engagement_affordance: a two-radar mission - watch a spaceship grid position and listen to call-signs at once, flag echoes in either channel; dual combos feel elite
adaptivity_fit: high - a single n scales both streams; auto-generated and essentially infinite
tail_discrimination: high - dual load produces a very high ceiling that strongly separates the gifted tail
coachability_bias_risk: a famous training target, so coachable; low cultural load; ADHD divided-attention lapses hit hard, so score consistency and lapse rate rather than best block
advantage_vs_cogat: a dual-stream updating construct plus rich two-channel error/RT telemetry that CogAT cannot approach
source_name: PEBL Test Battery - Dual N-Back (Jaeggi et al., 2008)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - open-source PEBL implementation; re-skin for children

item_format: Item type - a gamified child 2-back where a parade of picture characters passes and the child flags any character matching the one from two-ago
cognitive_process: updating and interference control with picture stimuli
engagement_affordance: a costume parade where characters march by and the child rings a bell when a costume repeats from two-ago; escalating tempo drives flow
adaptivity_fit: high - n and tempo scale; picture pools auto-generate for AIG
tail_discrimination: med - 2-back stretches bright grade 2-3 kids, but pace must be tuned to avoid floor/ceiling
coachability_bias_risk: low language load; motor/impulsivity confound in younger kids, so weight accuracy consistency; ADHD lapses should be modeled, not scored as raw speed
advantage_vs_cogat: brings an updating construct and lapse/RT-variability telemetry to a grade band CogAT under-serves
source_name: PsyToolkit experiment library - N-back (child adaptation)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - openly published base task; described here as a child-facing type to build

item_format: A list of items streams at a fixed rate and stops unpredictably; child must report the last few (n) items in order, forcing continuous updating of a rolling buffer
cognitive_process: continuous updating and maintenance of the most-recent items under uncertainty
engagement_affordance: a conveyor belt where items ride past and the belt stops without warning; the child grabs the last few still in view, rewarding always-ready updating
adaptivity_fit: high - list length, unknown stop point, and presentation rate are independent difficulty knobs, all auto-generated
tail_discrimination: high - an unpredictable endpoint and fast rates raise the ceiling and index updating linked to fluid intelligence
coachability_bias_risk: harder to game because the endpoint is hidden; low cultural load; ADHD lapses drop items, so measure updating consistency not peak speed
advantage_vs_cogat: an updating measure validated against fluid intelligence, with per-position accuracy telemetry CogAT lacks
source_name: Broadway & Engle (2010), Georgia Tech Attention & Working Memory Lab - running memory span
reuse_note: adapt_ok - freely provided for research; cite Broadway & Engle (2010)

item_format: Item type - any streamed sequence of unknown length where only the last-n must be recalled; presentation rate is tuned to force active updating (slow) versus passive readout (fast)
cognitive_process: strategy-sensitive updating versus focus-of-attention readout
engagement_affordance: tune the belt speed as a difficulty dial across grades - slow belts for young kids (active rehearsal), fast belts for older kids (attention readout)
adaptivity_fit: high - rate and length dials span the whole K-8 range from one template
tail_discrimination: high - fast and long conditions extend headroom for older gifted students
coachability_bias_risk: low coachability; strategy shifts with rate, so log presentation rate; attention lapses drop recent items, favor consistency scoring
advantage_vs_cogat: one updating paradigm that scales K-8 and emits position-level process data, unlike CogAT static reasoning items
source_name: Bunting/Ecker running-span updating literature - time course of updating in running span
reuse_note: adapt_ok - described paradigm; implement with our own stimuli and rate schedule

item_format: Alternating processing and storage - child verifies a simple math equation, then sees a letter to remember; after several cycles, recalls the letters in order (automated Operation Span)
cognitive_process: storage under concurrent processing (controlled attention / WM capacity)
engagement_affordance: a solve-and-stash quest - answer a quick puzzle to earn a gem, keep stashing gems, then place them in order on a treasure grid; distractor puzzles create real load
adaptivity_fit: high - set size and processing difficulty scale; fully automated generation and scoring
tail_discrimination: high - the dual demand yields strong separation and maps onto the latent WM-capacity/gF factor
coachability_bias_risk: the processing task limits pure rehearsal, lowering coachability; math load adds a small confound (control for arithmetic); ADHD lapses lower storage, weight consistency
advantage_vs_cogat: measures WM capacity under interference with processing-accuracy and recall telemetry; CogAT has no dual-task capacity measure
source_name: Georgia Tech Attention & Working Memory Lab - Automated Operation Span (Unsworth et al., 2005)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - free for research use; cite Unsworth et al. (2005)

item_format: Child judges whether a pattern is symmetrical (processing), then must remember a highlighted square location (storage); after several cycles, taps the square sequence in order
cognitive_process: visuospatial storage under a concurrent symmetry-judgment processing load
engagement_affordance: a mirror-check-then-mark game - kids thumbs-up symmetrical butterflies, then remember where stars appeared, recreating the constellation at trial end
adaptivity_fit: high - set size scales, symmetry stimuli auto-generate, scoring is automated
tail_discrimination: high - visuospatial dual load separates the top end and complements verbal complex spans
coachability_bias_risk: low language load; the symmetry judgment limits rehearsal; ADHD lapses drop locations, so favor consistency across set sizes over speed
advantage_vs_cogat: a visuospatial WM-capacity measure with processing-plus-recall process data absent from CogAT
source_name: Georgia Tech Attention & Working Memory Lab - Symmetry Span
reuse_note: adapt_ok - free for research; cite Unsworth/Redick complex-span papers

item_format: Child performs a mental-rotation judgment (processing) then remembers an arrow direction and length (storage); recalls the arrow sequence after several cycles
cognitive_process: spatial transformation processing with concurrent spatial storage
engagement_affordance: a spin-and-aim game - rotate a shape to check if it matches, then memorize where arrows point; fire the arrows back in order like a target-range combo
adaptivity_fit: high - set size and rotation angle scale difficulty over auto-generated trials
tail_discrimination: high - combines rotation and span load for strong high-end separation
coachability_bias_risk: low language/cultural load; rotation skill is partly trainable; ADHD lapses reduce storage, so score consistency not fastest rotations
advantage_vs_cogat: spatial-transformation plus WM-storage telemetry; CogAT figural items are untimed multiple choice with no process data
source_name: Georgia Tech Attention & Working Memory Lab - Rotation Span
reuse_note: adapt_ok - free for research; cite Kane/Unsworth complex-span work

item_format: Item type - child judges whether each sentence makes sense (processing), then holds a to-be-remembered word/letter (storage); recalls the set in order after several cycles
cognitive_process: verbal storage under a sentence-comprehension processing load
engagement_affordance: a sense-or-silly game - kids buzz whether a sentence is sensible, banking a word each time, then recite the banked words; silly sentences keep it playful
adaptivity_fit: med - set size scales, but sentence generation and reading level require authoring, capping AIG at younger grades
tail_discrimination: high for readers - the dual verbal load separates strong older students; not suitable pre-reading (K-1)
coachability_bias_risk: reading-ability confound (control for decoding); the processing step limits rehearsal; ADHD lapses lower storage, weight consistency
advantage_vs_cogat: verbal WM-capacity under comprehension load with dual process/recall telemetry CogAT does not collect
source_name: Georgia Tech Attention & Working Memory Lab - Reading Span (Daneman & Carpenter, 1980)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - free for research; requires reading, use for older bands

item_format: Item type (child complex span) - child counts target shapes on each card (processing) and remembers each count; after several cards, recalls the counts in order
cognitive_process: storage of tallies under a concurrent counting/processing load
engagement_affordance: a count-the-frogs game - tally frogs on each lily pad, remember each tally, then report the run of numbers; playful counting keeps young kids engaged
adaptivity_fit: high - set size and count range scale; cards auto-generate cheaply
tail_discrimination: med - counting complex span works young but ceilings earlier than operation/symmetry span
coachability_bias_risk: counting-fluency confound (control for it); low language load; young-child attention lapses expected, so score consistency across cards
advantage_vs_cogat: brings a dual-task WM-capacity measure to early grades with processing-plus-recall data; CogAT has no capacity measure at any age
source_name: Conway et al. (2005) complex-span user guide (counting span variant), via Georgia Tech lab
reuse_note: adapt_ok - described paradigm; build a picture-counting child version

item_format: Child is given a few categories (e.g., animals, foods) then sees a stream of words; at the end must report the most recent exemplar seen for each category, discarding older ones
cognitive_process: selective updating - overwrite old category values with newer ones
engagement_affordance: a keep-the-latest scoreboard - each category is a slot that visibly flips to the newest picture; kids race to report the current champions
adaptivity_fit: high - number of categories and stream length scale; word pools auto-generate
tail_discrimination: med - more categories raises load, but very high ceilings need many categories or fast pace
coachability_bias_risk: low cultural load; a light rehearsal strategy exists; ADHD lapses cause failure to overwrite, so score updating consistency not speed
advantage_vs_cogat: isolates selective updating with per-category error telemetry; CogAT measures neither updating nor error dynamics
source_name: Ecker, Lewandowsky & Oberauer (2010) - keep-track / memory updating tasks
reuse_note: adapt_ok - described paradigm; build with child-friendly categories

item_format: A small grid of digits is shown, then a series of arithmetic operations (e.g., +2) is applied to specific cells; child must track and report each cell final value
cognitive_process: maintenance plus repeated transformation/updating of stored values
engagement_affordance: a magic-cupboard game - each shelf holds a number and spells (+/-) change shelves; kids report what is on each shelf after the spells
adaptivity_fit: high - grid size, number of updates, and operation difficulty are independent knobs, all auto-generated
tail_discrimination: high - stacking updates on multiple cells pushes the ceiling and taxes transformation
coachability_bias_risk: arithmetic-skill confound (control for it); low language load; ADHD lapses cause stale values, so weight consistency across updates
advantage_vs_cogat: an updating-plus-transformation measure with step-level accuracy telemetry CogAT does not capture
source_name: Ecker, Lewandowsky & Oberauer (2010) - memory updating (matrix) task
reuse_note: adapt_ok - described paradigm; simplify operations for younger grades

item_format: Symbols appear one at a time; child must keep separate running counts of two or more target symbols and report the tallies on demand (symbol-counter)
cognitive_process: parallel maintenance and continuous incrementing of multiple counters
engagement_affordance: a tally-monster game - each monster eats its own snack type; kids keep each monster count in mind and feed back the totals when asked
adaptivity_fit: high - number of counters and stream speed scale; auto-generated symbol streams
tail_discrimination: high - tracking three or more counters at speed strongly separates the high end
coachability_bias_risk: low cultural load; finger-counting must be blocked; ADHD lapses derail counts, so measure consistency of tallies rather than raw speed
advantage_vs_cogat: multi-counter updating with per-counter error telemetry; CogAT has no comparable dynamic-load measure
source_name: PEBL Test Battery - Symbol Counter (Garavan, 1998)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - open-source PEBL task; re-skin as tally monsters

item_format: Frequent go stimuli require a fast tap while rare no-go stimuli require withholding the response; the high go rate builds a prepotent response that must be inhibited
cognitive_process: prepotent-response inhibition and sustained attention
engagement_affordance: a catch-the-fish, dodge-the-shark game - tap fast for fish (go) but freeze for the occasional shark (no-go); a broken combo on a shark stings just enough
adaptivity_fit: high - go/no-go ratio and pace scale difficulty; endless auto-generated trials
tail_discrimination: med - accuracy ceilings for older kids, but commission-error rate and RT variability keep discriminating
coachability_bias_risk: low cultural/language load; strongly ADHD-sensitive (commission errors track impulsivity), which is a confound - report false-alarm rate and consistency, and treat slow/lapse trials as signal, not speed
advantage_vs_cogat: yields inhibition-specific commission errors and RT-variability process data CogAT entirely lacks
source_name: PsyToolkit experiment library - Go/No-go task
reuse_note: adapt_ok - openly published task and code; re-skin as fish/shark

item_format: Item type - a parametric go/no-go where no-go probability and stimulus pacing are systematically varied to titrate inhibitory load across a wide ability range
cognitive_process: parametrically scaled response inhibition under attentional load
engagement_affordance: a dial-the-difficulty arcade - sharks get rarer and faster as kids improve, so inhibition demand ramps like arcade waves
adaptivity_fit: high - no-go rate and pace are explicit continuous difficulty parameters, ideal for adaptive staircasing
tail_discrimination: high - rarer, faster no-go trials create the surprise that separates strong inhibitors at the top
coachability_bias_risk: low cultural load; ADHD/impulsivity confound is central - interpret commission errors as attention signal; weight lapse consistency over peak reaction speed
advantage_vs_cogat: a titratable inhibition construct with parametric difficulty and error/RT telemetry CogAT cannot match
source_name: PsyToolkit experiment library - Go/No-go (parametric variant)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - openly published base task; described as a parametric type to build

item_format: A central target arrow is flanked by arrows pointing the same (congruent) or opposite (incongruent) way; child responds to the center only, suppressing the flankers
cognitive_process: selective attention and interference suppression (conflict resolution)
engagement_affordance: a which-way-is-the-middle-fish-swimming game - a row of fish, only the middle one counts; incongruent rows create playful confusion
adaptivity_fit: high - congruency ratio and pace scale; endless auto-generated arrays
tail_discrimination: med - accuracy ceilings, but the congruent-minus-incongruent RT conflict cost keeps discriminating at the top
coachability_bias_risk: low language/cultural load; ADHD attention confound inflates the conflict cost; use the interference score and RT consistency rather than raw speed
advantage_vs_cogat: a conflict-cost (interference) metric and RT telemetry CogAT never produces
source_name: PsyToolkit experiment library - Flanker task
reuse_note: adapt_ok - openly published task and code; re-skin as swimming fish

item_format: Item type - a child fish-flanker where the child indicates the direction of the central fish while ignoring flanking fish; a standardized version spans early childhood
cognitive_process: inhibitory control and selective attention with child-friendly stimuli
engagement_affordance: the classic swimming-fish flanker kids already enjoy - point where the middle fish swims; friendly art lowers anxiety for young testers
adaptivity_fit: med - the standardized form has fixed blocks, but the paradigm clones easily with new congruent/incongruent art
tail_discrimination: med - designed for developmental sensitivity rather than a high gifted ceiling; conflict cost adds some headroom
coachability_bias_risk: low cultural load; ADHD attention confound is well documented; rely on the interference score and consistency, not peak speed
advantage_vs_cogat: a normed early-childhood inhibition measure with a conflict-cost score CogAT lacks; a model for our own child flanker
source_name: NIH Toolbox - Flanker Inhibitory Control and Attention Test
reuse_note: describe_only - secure credentialed instrument; describe/link and build our own fish flanker

item_format: Color words are printed in mismatched ink colors; child must name/select the ink color while suppressing the automatic urge to read the word
cognitive_process: prepotent-response (reading) inhibition and interference control
engagement_affordance: a paint-not-read game - kids tap the ink color of tricky words; a mischievous word tries to trick them, and beating it earns points
adaptivity_fit: high - congruency mix and pace scale; auto-generated word/color combos
tail_discrimination: med - accuracy ceilings, but the Stroop interference cost (incongruent minus congruent RT) discriminates at the top
coachability_bias_risk: requires reading fluency (confound - control for decoding); modest cultural load; ADHD lapses swell the interference cost, so score consistency not raw speed
advantage_vs_cogat: a classic interference-cost metric plus RT telemetry CogAT never captures
source_name: PsyToolkit experiment library - Stroop task
reuse_note: adapt_ok - Stroop is a public paradigm with openly published code; adapt for readers

item_format: Pairs of digits differ in numeric value and physical size; child must judge one dimension (e.g., which is numerically larger) while ignoring the conflicting dimension
cognitive_process: dimensional interference control between magnitude and size
engagement_affordance: a bigger-number-wins duel where the digits grow and shrink to trick you; ignoring the size feint and picking the true value feels like a skill move
adaptivity_fit: high - congruency and pace scale; digit pairs auto-generate endlessly
tail_discrimination: med/high - the size-value conflict cost extends discrimination for numerate older kids
coachability_bias_risk: number-knowledge confound (control for it); low language load; ADHD lapses enlarge the conflict cost, so weight consistency over speed
advantage_vs_cogat: a numerical interference-cost measure with RT telemetry; CogAT quantitative items are untimed and yield no conflict data
source_name: PsyToolkit experiment library - Numerical Stroop task
reuse_note: adapt_ok - openly published task; use for numerate older grades

item_format: Child must say night to a sun picture and day to a moon picture - a Stroop-like task requiring inhibition of the obvious semantic response, designed for pre/early readers
cognitive_process: suppression of a prepotent semantic response with a rule in working memory
engagement_affordance: an opposite-day game - the sun means say night and the moon means say day; the silliness makes the inhibition demand feel like a joke to master
adaptivity_fit: med - few stimulus types cap raw AIG, but pacing and added opposite-pairs extend it
tail_discrimination: low/med - built for young developmental sensitivity; add speeded blocks or more pairs to lift the ceiling
coachability_bias_risk: very low reading/culture load (ideal for K-1); some rule-learning practice; ADHD lapses cause rule slips, so score accuracy consistency, not speed
advantage_vs_cogat: a language-light inhibition measure at a grade CogAT barely assesses, with error-pattern data CogAT lacks
source_name: Gerstadt, Hong & Diamond (1994) day-night task - review
reuse_note: adapt_ok - classic public child paradigm; build with our own sun/moon art

item_format: Item type - child responds quickly to a go stimulus, but on a minority of trials a stop signal appears after a variable delay and the already-initiated response must be cancelled, estimating stop-signal reaction time
cognitive_process: reactive inhibition - cancelling an in-flight motor response (action restraint vs cancellation)
engagement_affordance: a slam-the-brakes racing game - accelerate on go, but hit the brakes when the stoplight flashes; a staircased delay keeps it right at the edge of control
adaptivity_fit: high - the stop-signal delay auto-staircases to a target 50 percent inhibition, a naturally adaptive design
tail_discrimination: high - stop-signal reaction time is a continuous latent metric with strong high-end resolution
coachability_bias_risk: low cultural load; strongly ADHD-sensitive (a core impulsivity marker) - a confound to model; report SSRT and its consistency, and note slow/lapse go-trials as signal
advantage_vs_cogat: produces a modeled inhibition latency (SSRT) - a process metric CogAT cannot generate
source_name: CANTAB - Stop Signal Task (SST), Cambridge Cognition
reuse_note: describe_only - proprietary battery; open stop-signal variants exist to adapt instead

item_format: Item type - across timed subtests the child names shapes/directions against a prepotent response (Inhibition) and holds a body position with eyes closed while ignoring sound distractors (Statue) for younger children
cognitive_process: response inhibition and motor persistence/self-regulation
engagement_affordance: describe-only; a freeze-like-a-statue mini-game plus a say-the-opposite naming race maps directly onto the child-facing versions we could build
adaptivity_fit: med - fixed secure subtests and age ranges; the underlying motor-inhibition idea clones well for young grades
tail_discrimination: med - developmentally graded rather than tuned for a high gifted ceiling
coachability_bias_risk: low cultural load; ADHD-sensitive by design (a confound); the timed naming yields error-plus-time data, so favor consistency over raw speed
advantage_vs_cogat: a standardized child inhibition/self-regulation battery with timed error data CogAT does not collect
source_name: NEPSY-II - Inhibition and Statue subtests, Pearson
reuse_note: describe_only - secure copyrighted battery; model the format only

item_format: Item type - a timed color-word interference test with an inhibition condition (name the ink color) and an inhibition/switching condition (alternate between naming the ink and reading the word)
cognitive_process: verbal inhibition plus set-shifting (combined interference and switching)
engagement_affordance: describe-only; a two-mode paint-or-read race where a rule flips mid-run maps onto a gamified inhibition-plus-switch level we could design
adaptivity_fit: med - fixed secure conditions and stimulus book; the inhibition/switch structure clones with new color-word sets
tail_discrimination: med/high - the switching condition and completion-time contrasts add headroom for older students
coachability_bias_risk: reading confound (baseline conditions parcel it out); low cultural load; ADHD lapses lengthen completion time, so use condition contrasts and consistency, not raw speed
advantage_vs_cogat: separates inhibition from switching via timed condition contrasts - process data CogAT cannot yield
source_name: D-KEFS - Color-Word Interference Test, Pearson
reuse_note: describe_only - secure copyrighted battery; model the condition structure only

item_format: Child sorts bivalent cards (e.g., red rabbits, blue boats) first by one rule (color), then is told to switch to the other rule (shape); post-switch sorting indexes flexibility
cognitive_process: cognitive flexibility - shifting between conflicting sorting rules while resisting perseveration
engagement_affordance: a sort-the-toys-then-flip-the-rule game - drag cards to bins by color, then a whistle flips the rule to shape; beating the old habit is the fun
adaptivity_fit: high - rule dimensions, switch frequency, and (border version) mixed cues scale difficulty; art auto-generates
tail_discrimination: med - most 5+ pass the standard switch; the border/mixed version and RT costs extend discrimination upward
coachability_bias_risk: very low language load; some rule-learning practice; ADHD lapses cause perseverative errors, so score switch-cost consistency rather than speed
advantage_vs_cogat: a set-shifting construct with perseverative-error and switch-cost telemetry entirely outside CogAT scope
source_name: Zelazo (2006) Dimensional Change Card Sort (DCCS), Nature Protocols
reuse_note: adapt_ok - published protocol, widely reproduced; build with our own picture cards

item_format: Item type - the border/advanced DCCS where a border cue on each card signals which rule applies trial-by-trial, forcing rapid cue-driven switching for older preschool/early-primary children
cognitive_process: cue-based rule switching with trial-by-trial conflict
engagement_affordance: a decoder-badge game - a colored border tells kids which rule is live this turn, so every card is a fresh switch decision with a beat-the-clock feel
adaptivity_fit: high - border-cue frequency and pace scale; the mixed design supports fine adaptive tuning
tail_discrimination: high - trial-by-trial mixed switching produces switch-cost variance that separates strong flexers
coachability_bias_risk: low language load; ADHD lapses inflate switch errors (a confound), so use switch-cost and its consistency, not raw speed
advantage_vs_cogat: trial-level switch costs and mixing costs - dynamic process data CogAT does not provide
source_name: Zelazo (2006) DCCS border version, Nature Protocols; Millisecond library
reuse_note: adapt_ok - published paradigm with open task scripts; build our own cued version

item_format: Item type - a computerized DCCS where the child matches a series of picture pairs to a target, switching the matching rule (shape vs color) as instructed, scored for accuracy and reaction time
cognitive_process: cognitive flexibility and attention with combined accuracy/RT scoring
engagement_affordance: describe-only; the tablet card-flip switch game already feels like an app level and shows how to fold accuracy-plus-speed scoring into engagement
adaptivity_fit: med - the standardized computerized form is fixed, but the paradigm generalizes for AIG
tail_discrimination: med - designed across a wide age span; the RT-weighted score adds headroom over accuracy alone
coachability_bias_risk: low cultural load; ADHD attention confound; the combined accuracy-plus-RT scoring should emphasize consistency, treating lapse trials as signal
advantage_vs_cogat: a normed switching measure with combined accuracy-and-latency scoring CogAT lacks; a model for our own switch task
source_name: NIH Toolbox - Dimensional Change Card Sort Test
reuse_note: describe_only - secure credentialed instrument; describe/link and build our own version

item_format: On each trial a number-letter pair appears; the child does the letter task (vowel/consonant) or number task (odd/even) depending on position, alternating in predictable runs (alternating-runs switching)
cognitive_process: task-set reconfiguration - switching between two active rule sets
engagement_affordance: a two-lane game where the character jumps lanes on a rhythm; each lane needs a different rule, so switching lanes on the beat is the challenge
adaptivity_fit: high - run length, cue support, and pace scale; endless auto-generated pairs
tail_discrimination: high - the switch cost (switch minus repeat RT) is a sensitive continuous metric with a high ceiling
coachability_bias_risk: low cultural load; some practice reduces switch cost; ADHD lapses enlarge it (a confound), so score switch-cost consistency, not peak speed
advantage_vs_cogat: an explicit switch-cost metric plus repeat/switch RT telemetry CogAT cannot produce
source_name: PsyToolkit experiment library - Task switching (alternating runs, Rogers & Monsell)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - openly published task and code; simplify rules for younger grades

item_format: A cue before each trial tells the child which of two tasks to perform on the upcoming stimulus, so switches occur unpredictably and cue-encoding time is isolated (cued task switching)
cognitive_process: cue-driven task-set reconfiguration with unpredictable switches
engagement_affordance: a spy-mission game - a flashed code tells you which gadget rule to use this round; unpredictable orders keep players on their toes
adaptivity_fit: high - cue-stimulus interval, switch rate, and pace scale; fully auto-generated
tail_discrimination: high - unpredictable cued switches yield large switch and mixing costs that separate the top end
coachability_bias_risk: low cultural load; ADHD lapses inflate switch/mixing costs (a confound); use cost contrasts and consistency, not raw speed
advantage_vs_cogat: decomposes switching into cue-encoding and reconfiguration via RT contrasts - process data CogAT lacks
source_name: PsyToolkit experiment library - Task switching (cued version)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - openly published task and code; re-skin as a spy mission

item_format: Item type - child sorts cards to piles by an unstated rule (color, shape, or number), discovering the rule from feedback; the rule changes without warning, requiring a shift (Berg/Wisconsin card sorting)
cognitive_process: rule induction from feedback plus set-shifting and perseveration control
engagement_affordance: a crack-the-secret-rule game - kids deduce the hidden sorting rule from thumbs-up/down, then must notice when the rule silently changes and adapt
adaptivity_fit: med - category count and rule-change schedule scale; the discovery element limits pure AIG cloning
tail_discrimination: high - perseverative-error and categories-completed metrics separate flexible high-ability sorters
coachability_bias_risk: low cultural load; once the trick is known it is coachable, so vary rules; ADHD lapses raise perseverative errors, favor consistency scoring
advantage_vs_cogat: yields perseverative-error and rule-shift metrics (executive process data) CogAT never captures
source_name: PEBL Test Battery - Berg/Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (BCST)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - open-source PEBL implementation; re-skin for children

item_format: Item type - child learns which stimulus feature is rewarded and must shift within a dimension (intra-dimensional) and later across dimensions (extra-dimensional), isolating attentional set-shifting
cognitive_process: attentional set formation and intra/extra-dimensional shifting
engagement_affordance: describe-only; a learn-the-winning-feature game that later forces a leap to a whole new feature type maps onto a staged puzzle we could build
adaptivity_fit: high - staged shift structure has clear graded levels for adaptive progression
tail_discrimination: high - the extra-dimensional shift stage is a well-known high-resolution flexibility marker
coachability_bias_risk: low cultural load; ADHD-sensitive (a confound); report stage reached and errors with consistency, not raw speed
advantage_vs_cogat: separates within- from across-dimension shifting - a fine-grained flexibility profile CogAT cannot give
source_name: CANTAB - Intra-Extra Dimensional Set Shift (IED), Cambridge Cognition
reuse_note: describe_only - proprietary battery; build a staged set-shift analog instead

item_format: Child plays a game of doing the opposite of a spoken command (touch your head when told toes), with new rules added and switched, integrating working memory, inhibition, and shifting
cognitive_process: holding rules in working memory while inhibiting the natural motor response and switching when rules change
engagement_affordance: an embodied opposite-day movement game - kids giggle doing the reverse action; adding knees/shoulders rules ramps the challenge like new dance moves
adaptivity_fit: med - rule count and switching scale, but scoring is observer-based and motoric, limiting fully automated AIG
tail_discrimination: med - added rules and rule-switches extend the range; a revised downward extension reduces floors for the youngest
coachability_bias_risk: very low language/reading and materials load; ADHD self-regulation confound is central; score self-corrections and consistency, not speed
advantage_vs_cogat: an embodied, materials-free integrated-EF measure with error/self-correction data at a grade CogAT under-serves
source_name: Head-Toes-Knees-Shoulders (HTKS) task, Ponitz/McClelland - Vanderbilt protocol
